title: A logger that builds messages only when it is switched on

blocks.text: Building a log message (formatting, joining, `toString()` on big objects) costs time even when the message is then thrown away. A logger that takes a `Supplier<String>` builds the text only when it will be used. A feature switch is a natural `BooleanSupplier`: `boolean getAsBoolean()`, no boxing.

items: `debug(Supplier<String> message)` records `message.get()` if the switch is on at that moment.
`lines()` returns the recorded messages, oldest first.

blocks.text: The switch may change while the program runs. Each enabled `debug` builds its message exactly once and records it as it is, repeats and `null` included. `lines()` returns a snapshot: later `debug` calls do not change a list it returned earlier.

cases.says: While the switch is on, each message is built and recorded in order.
While the switch is off, the message Supplier is never called.
The switch is asked on every debug call, so turning it on later takes effect.
A list returned by lines() keeps its contents when more messages are logged later.
An enabled debug call builds its message exactly once and records it as it is, even when it is null.

concepts: BooleanSupplier answers a primitive boolean through getAsBoolean, which suits a switch read on demand.
A Supplier's work runs only when get() is called, and not at all if nobody asks.
